name: Vista Flota
imageAlt: High-level architecture diagram of the Vista Flota platform on Google Cloud
summary: A real-time IoT fleet platform: a device on each truck publishes telemetry over MQTT — position, speed, fuel — which the platform ingests, deduplicates and turns into live fleet state, trips and alerts on an operator dashboard, archiving the full history for route reconstruction.
highlights: The requirement was 1,000 events/s sustained with zero message loss. The baseline architecture died of OOM at 80.

Removed bottlenecks one at a time — measure, diagnose, fix, re-validate — with Prometheus and Grafana: deduplication moved out of PostgreSQL into Redis, PgBouncer multiplexing 200 client connections over 20 real ones, watermark-based backpressure, MQTT QoS 1, and KEDA replaced by HPA once profiling proved the pods were CPU-bound.
Final result: 5,000 events/s at peak, 3,200 sustained, 0.00% loss.
note: Team project across three areas (Application, Infrastructure, IoT). I owned the Application area. Repository is private.

name: AI report generation
tagline: Hours of manual writing, down to seconds
summary: IDDIGO tracks over 1,000 indicators per territory, but reading them and turning them into a written analysis was manual work for the client. I designed and built from scratch the feature that does it automatically.
highlights: The interesting part isn't the API call — it's deciding what context goes into the prompt and what stays out, and keeping that decision cheap and bounded as the indicator catalogue grows.
Built the layer that gathers and structures the platform's full data context, then calls Google Gemini to produce the report.
What users previously had to write by hand is now generated in seconds.

name: Embeddable widget
tagline: The same product, running inside someone else's site
summary: A business constraint — clients wanted IDDIGO inside their own websites — that turned into an architecture problem: how do you embed a full application in a third-party domain without duplicating the product?
highlights: Converted the Angular application into a component embeddable in third-party sites.
Required rebuilding authentication from the ground up to work under a domain we don't control.
